newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Interbrew seeks help on Canadian assets.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Interbrew seeks help on Canadian assets.

text.p: Belgian brewing giant Interbrew said on Thursday that it was still seeking partners for sporting assets owned by its Canadian unit Labatt Brewing Co Ltd and "a number" of parties were interested.

The assets concerned are Labatt's 90 percent share of the Toronto Blue Jays baseball club; its 100 percent share of the Toronto Argonauts -- a club in the Canadian football league -- and an interest in Toronto's 50,000-seat SkyDome stadium.
"There are three businesses with different goals and different shareholders," said Hugo Powell, Interbrew's chief operating officer for the Americas region.
"We are interested in bringing new partners into those business. We are looking for local partners for them all."
Until any deals were reached, the priority was to run them well and profitably, he added.
Powell, who was speaking at a presentation of Interbrew's 1996 results, said the value of Labatt's share in the three had been estimated by others at a US$185 million.

Interbrew acquired the assets when it bought Labatt in July 1995. It had said it wanted to concentrate on the core brewing business, though it was in no rush to sell the sports assets and it envisaged retaining the marketing rights.
